title: Weeks of waiting in the Manila staging area for instruments
summary: Their instruments went missing for two or three weeks, during which about fifty shows lived like a family in the staging area without working.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Well, they got set up there, and we are just browsing around, waiting for orders. No orders have come in. And then we come to find the plane with the instruments and things hadn't shown up. We were there, but the plane with the instruments, they hadn't shown up. They don't know where the instruments and things are. So we're just layin'

around, eatin' and sleepin', and enjoying ourself the best we can. What else is there to do? You can't mope about no instruments, because Uncle Sam had plenty of instruments to furnish us. If they don't show up, they have big warehouses, big as Madison Square Garden, full of nothin' but instruments. We wasn't worried about the instruments. But the point is, ours just didn't show up on the plane.
But everybody had brought his own instrument, really, hadn't they? I mean, these weren't...
Yeah, but these weren't instruments that had been issued to you. They were your own.
No, these are our own personal instruments.
Your very own personal instruments, yeah.

So anyway, these instruments... I mean, they held up everything. I think we were around... I know exactly how long we were there. We didn't do anything for about two or three weeks, and just eatin' and sleepin'. And one day, the instruments did show up. They finally got there. Well, we're still waiting for orders. So we're still enjoying life. And there's plenty of life in Manila, too. Oh, Manila was just like New York. Meeting the people there, one-thing-or-another, nightclubs... Everything. Stores. Cities. Bombed-out cities and one-thing-or-
another. But life was goin' on, moving.
Well, I was not the one to venture forth into anything. I stayed right around the staging area, and there wasn't a whole lot of moving for me. I didn't care for it that much.

So there was about fifty different shows stationed in the staging area, shows of one person, one-man shows, up to shows of fifty personnel, big shows. And we was all around the staging area... It was just like a family. And we'd get together, and we'd talk, this-that-and-the-other, and play different games, and sports and one-thing-or-another. And had a ball, you know. At night, some of the shows, they'd go up, we'd do the shows and things, then come back, and get in the games and one-thing-or-another. We really had a good time! So I said, 'Oh, this is not bad at all.' No, no. We hadn't hit a drop of work yet.
